newsitem.title: UK: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.9 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.9 pct in June.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following retail price indices for June:
RETAIL PRICES INDEX JUNE MAY JUNE 96
Mth pct change ex MIPs, tax 0.3 0.3 0.1
COMPONENT DETAILS OF THE ALL-ITEMS INDEX (PCT CHANGES) -
NOTE - Consensus forecast was RPI up 0.2 pct MM, +2.8 pct YY RPIX +2.5 pct YY, RPIY +2.0 pct YY.
* The headline year-on-year rate of RPI, at 2.9 percent, was the highest since January 1996.
** The 5.0 percent rise in monthly seasonal food prices was the first rise in a June since 1991 and the largest June rise since 1978.
For housing, the annual rate of 6.0 percent was the highest since September 1995.
The annual rate of household goods prices was the lowest since February 1997 and was last lower in October 1994.
The ONS said the increase in the all items 12-month rate was largely due to rises in housing costs. Other significant upward pressures came from seasonal food prices and motoring costs.
There were, however, significant downward effects from alcoholic drinks' prices and fuel and light prices. Smaller downward pressures came from household goods and clothing and footwear.

For clothing and footwear, the start of some early summer sales outweighed continuing increases as new stock entered the shops. Childrens' clothing, in particular, showed a sharp price fall over the month.
For household goods, furniture prices failed to rise as sharply as they did in June last year and electrical appliance prices fell more in price last month than they did in June 1996.
